_note: Voices approved by Ryan 2026-10-16. voice_id is the ElevenLabs library id; each must be added to the account's voices (My Voices > Add) before Text-to-Dialogue can use it. Never change a voice_id once episodes are published.

characters.name: Lehua
characters.voice_brief: Warm, quick, local Hawaiʻi cadence, laughs easily, keeps the show moving. Not a radio voice, a cool older-cousin voice.
characters.gag: Always has a Costco run to get to after the show. Facts to keep straight: Kona Costco (73-5600 Maiau St) is open seven days, closes 8:30 PM Mon to Fri, 7:00 PM Sat, 6:00 PM Sun; about an hour from Waimea. The joke is the drive and the early Sunday close, never that it is closed.
characters.speaks: Light pidgin seasoning, standard English for the teaching parts.

characters.name: Derek Nakamura
characters.voice_brief: Dry, precise, calm, slightly deadpan. Japanese-American local, Hilo-raised. The guy who says the shortcut once and waits.
characters.gag: Rates every shortcut out of ten and nothing has ever scored a ten.
characters.speaks: Standard English throughout, occasional local phrasing in banter only.

characters.name: Sarah Medeiros
characters.voice_brief: Storyteller energy, expressive, Portuguese-Hawaiian local, grammar nerd who is funny about it. Clear diction.
characters.gag: Cannot let a misplaced comma go, even in a text from her mom.

characters.name: Coach Pono
characters.voice_brief: Ex-paniolo, ex-track coach, big easy voice, talks about the clock like a horse you have to manage. Hawaiian, Waimea-born.
characters.gag: Every strategy is secretly a rodeo metaphor.
characters.speaks: Pidgin-forward in banter; every teaching line in standard English, slowed down.

characters.name: Kaden
characters.voice_brief: Gen Z, honest, asks the question everyone is thinking, a little sleepy at the top of the show and locked in by the end. Local mixed kid.
characters.gag: Relates everything to a game, a car, or being late for the bus.
characters.speaks: Gen Z slang in moderation, pidgin when excited.

style_rules: Pidgin and local slang only for characters marked local, and only in conversational banter (greetings, jokes, reactions, transitions).
Teaching lines (any sentence that states a rule, a number, a formula, a strategy step, or a definition) are standard English for every character, including Coach Pono.
Standard English means no 'wen', 'stay', 'da', 'dis', 'get' for 'have', or dropped copulas inside an instructional sentence.
A character can set up a teaching point in pidgin ('Okay, listen up, dis one important') and then deliver the point itself in standard English.
_pronunciation: 2026-10-16 finding: dictionaries (alias and IPA) do not fix Hawaiian on ElevenLabs. Mikey (Coach Pono) pronounces Hawaiian correctly from raw spelling on eleven_v3. render2.py renders Pono whole and splices termbank clips (Pono's voice) into other characters' Hawaiian words.
fact_rules: Any real place, business, hour, price, or date mentioned in a script must be verified before rendering and noted in the script header as 'facts:'.
